blocks.text: The docstring explains why folder trust exists: a cloned repository is attacker-controlled content, and project settings / hooks / skills inside it have elevated power. Nothing in those files takes effect until the user grants trust, and trust is voided if any covered file changes.
blocks.title: Package docstring: the folder-trust security model

blocks.text: The docstring lists fingerprint.py (SHA-256 over covered files), prompt.py (the UI-facing trust question), and store.py (persistence of the granted/denied answer). This inline documentation serves as the package-level table of contents.
blocks.title: Inline index of the three submodules

blocks.text: Star-imports everything from fingerprint.py into the m2c.trust namespace. Callers who need to compute or compare a folder fingerprint can import from m2c.trust directly without knowing the submodule name.
blocks.title: Re-export: fingerprint

blocks.text: prompt.py exports the user-facing trust prompt UI helpers; store.py exports the functions that read and write the persisted trust decision. Both are pulled into the top-level m2c.trust namespace by star-imports.
blocks.title: Re-export: prompt and store

how_it_works: Three star-imports re-export all public names from fingerprint.py (SHA-256 over covered files), prompt.py (the UI prompt asking the user to grant trust), and store.py (persistence of the trust answer).
The file uses only the standard library — no third-party dependencies are introduced at this layer.
purpose: Implements Patch C26 (folder trust). A project folder is attacker-controlled content; certain files in it (project settings, hooks, skills) have elevated power. Nothing in them is used until the user explicitly says 'I trust this folder', and that answer holds only while the covered files stay exactly as they were when trust was granted.
summary: Package init for m2c/trust/: re-exports everything from fingerprint.py, prompt.py and store.py so callers import directly from m2c.trust.
unknowns: Which specific files in a project folder are considered 'covered' (high-power) is defined in fingerprint.py, not visible here.
How and where store.py persists the trust decision (disk, keychain, etc.) is not shown in this file.
